newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends in minus column, support intact.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends in minus column, support intact.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures ended with small losses on arbitrage and light origin selling but the downside was supported by keen roaster demand.
By the close, benchmark November was $5 off at $1,525 a tonne after sinking to the key $1,520 support at one stage due to light origin selling.
"The market is not running from the support area but it is not really collapsing," said one.
Volume was 3,284 lots, with some activity centred on switches.
In structure, Sept/Nov was traded at $80 and Nov/Jan was dealt in the $50-$55 area and even up to $58.
"The switches were quite firm and this helped put some stability in the market," said a trader.
Interest was also seen in the options pit, where November $1,700 calls were dealt at $15.
"It seems that some of the trade wants to buy some calls as an upside protection may be against their short positions in case the market goes up," the trader said.
Immediately, traders said the market direction would hinge on New York's trend.
"London will watch New York and if New York fails, London will follow," one said.
